transcript.content: Thank you for calling Sky Airways customer service. My name is Sky, and I'm here to help you today. How can I assist you?

"Hi Sky, thanks for answering. My name is Rachel Wilson, and I'm actually planning a trip to Athens in about two months' time. I was wondering if you could let me know what kind of wheelchair assistance is available for passengers like myself who need extra help getting on and off the plane?"
Certainly, Rachel. I can help you with that. To provide you with the most accurate information, I'll look up our special assistance policy regarding wheelchairs.

"That sounds great, thank you for checking on it for me. Before we proceed, just to confirm, you'd be able to assist me in getting my wheelchair to the gate and helping me get seated, right, or would I need to request additional assistance with things like finding a suitable seat or accessing the aircraft itself?"

Rachel, based on our policy, we offer different levels of wheelchair assistance to ensure your comfort and safety.

For your needs, where you require assistance getting your wheelchair to the gate and help getting seated, the WCHS (Wheelchair to Seat) service would be most appropriate. This service provides assistance from check-in all the way to your seat on the aircraft. This includes help with accessing the aircraft and getting settled into your seat.

Additionally, passengers with reduced mobility are pre-assigned suitable seating free of charge, and bulkhead seats with extra legroom are available upon request.

Please remember that special assistance needs to be requested at least 48 hours before departure.

"Okay, that sounds great. So just to confirm, I would need to request the WCHS service and let you know my specific seating requirements in advance, and if I don't provide that notice within 48 hours of the flight, it might not be available for me? And are there any additional fees associated with this service beyond what's included in my ticket price?"

That's correct, Rachel. You would need to request the WCHS service, and you can also let us know your seating preferences, such as a bulkhead seat with extra legroom, in advance.

It's important to request this special assistance at least 48 hours before your flight's departure. While we always do our best to accommodate, providing less notice might mean we cannot guarantee the full range of assistance you require.

Regarding fees, I'm happy to confirm that special assistance services, including WCHS, are provided free of charge by Sky Airways. The only exception is for unaccompanied minors.

"Great, that's a relief to know it's included in my ticket price. Just to make sure I understand, can I request the WCHS service online or will I need to contact you directly through this call? And if I need anything at all during the flight, like extra assistance with using the lavatory or something, would that be covered under the same service?"

You can request the WCHS service either by contacting us directly, like on this call, or you can add it when you book your flight online.

Regarding assistance during the flight, the WCHS service primarily covers assistance from check-in to your seat on the aircraft. This includes help with boarding and disembarking. For assistance with personal needs during the flight, such as using the lavatory, our cabin crew can provide general support, but they are not able to provide extensive personal care. If you anticipate needing significant assistance with personal care during the flight, we recommend traveling with a companion.

"Alright, I think I have it covered then. Just to confirm, if I book online and select WCHS service, will my contact information be shared with the cabin crew so that they can prepare accordingly for my arrival at the gate, or would I still need to notify them of any specific needs I may have during the flight?"

When you book online and select the WCHS service, this information is attached to your booking. Our ground staff and cabin crew are made aware of passengers requiring special assistance, including WCHS, so they can prepare accordingly for your arrival at the gate and during the boarding process.

While the crew will be aware that you require wheelchair assistance, it's always a good idea to communicate any specific needs you may have during the flight directly to the cabin crew once you are on board. This ensures they can provide the best possible support for you.

"Okay, got it. I think that makes sense. So just to confirm one more thing, since I'll need assistance with both getting to my seat and using a wheelchair throughout the flight, is there any specific information or documentation that I would need to provide ahead of time, such as a doctor's note or something?"

For the WCHS service, which covers assistance from check-in to your seat, a doctor's note is not typically required. The main requirement is to provide us with at least 48 hours' notice so we can arrange the necessary assistance.

However, if you have a medical condition that might require specific medical equipment during the flight, or if you have a condition that could be affected by air travel, it's always a good idea to consult with your doctor and inform us if there are any special considerations. But for standard wheelchair assistance (WCHS), advance notice is usually sufficient.

"Alright, that makes sense. I think I'll go talk to my doctor just in case, but it sounds like the 48-hour notice is all that's required for the WCHS service. Is there a contact number or email address where I can notify you of my need for assistance if I decide to book online?"

I cannot provide a direct contact number or email address through this chat. However, if you book online, you will typically find an option to add special assistance during the booking process itself. If you've already booked and need to add assistance, you can usually manage your booking on the Sky Airways website, where you'll find sections for adding special services or contact information for our accessibility team.
"Okay, I understand. That makes sense. Well, I think that's all the questions I have for now, thank you so much for your help and guidance on getting the WCHS service. Perfect, thank you so much."

evaluation.summary: Agent understood the request and provided accurate information about wheelchair assistance services.
